items.title: Create leaf core/digest.ts with the canonical-JSON-digest primitives
items.context: New packages/main/src/core/digest.ts exporting Digestable, canonicalJson, digestCanonicalJson, digestText (and normalizeJson as needed), extracted verbatim from decision-doc-promotion.ts lines 64-88. Leaf module: imports only node:crypto. Digest values must be byte-identical to the originals.
items.userSees: Build clean; core/digest.ts exists; the smoke asserts digestCanonicalJson/canonicalJson/digestText produce the exact same output as a pinned set of inputs (byte-identical to pre-refactor).

happy.desc: core/digest.ts exists at packages/main/src/core/digest.ts and exports Digestable, canonicalJson, digestCanonicalJson, digestText, normalizeJson; WHY: verifies the file was created with all required symbols
canonicalJson({b:1,a:2}) produces identical JSON to pre-refactor inline version (keys sorted: {a:2,b:1}); WHY: proves canonicalization is stable after extraction
digestCanonicalJson({b:1,a:2}) returns the same SHA-256 hex as sha256(canonicalJson({b:1,a:2})); WHY: proves digest is byte-identical to pre-refactor on a pinned input
digestText('hello') returns sha256 hex of 'hello'; WHY: proves text digest is byte-identical to pre-refactor

edge.desc: canonicalJson with deeply nested object with reordered keys at every level produces stable sorted output; WHY: canonicalization must be recursive, not just top-level
canonicalJson with null, boolean, number, string, and array values normalizes correctly (null stays null, arrays preserve order); WHY: boundary on all JSON primitive types
canonicalJson with undefined-valued keys omits them from output; WHY: undefined is not valid JSON and must be stripped for canonical form
digestCanonicalJson on empty object {} returns deterministic sha256 of '{}'; WHY: edge case for minimal valid input
digestText on empty string returns sha256 of empty string; WHY: empty-input edge case

adversarial.desc: core/digest.ts imports only node:crypto and nothing else (grep import lines); WHY: leaf-module constraint -- if it imports anything else the dependency tree is violated and future consumers inherit unwanted deps
canonicalJson with deeply nested structure (100 levels) does not crash and produces deterministic output; WHY: adversarial deep nesting stress test on recursive normalizeJson

digestCanonicalJson and digestText produce DIFFERENT hashes for the same string input -- digestCanonicalJson wraps in JSON.stringify quotes, digestText does not; WHY: proves the two functions are semantically distinct and not accidentally interchangeable

verificationEvidence.note: core/digest.ts is a leaf (node:crypto only) exporting the digest primitives; smoke asserts byte-identical pinned digests + order-independence + digestText!=digestCanonicalJson.

items.title: Refactor decision-doc-promotion.ts to import the digest primitives from core/digest.ts
items.context: Replace the inline normalizeJson/canonicalJson/digestCanonicalJson/digestText definitions in handlers/decision-doc-promotion.ts with imports from ../core/digest.js. No behaviour change: computeDecisionDocProposalDigest / digestDecision produce identical values; existing decision-doc proposals stay valid.
items.userSees: decision-doc-promotion.ts imports from ../core/digest.js; its existing smoke/behaviour is unchanged; no digest value changes.

happy.desc: decision-doc-promotion.ts contains import statement from '../core/digest.js' for canonicalJson, digestCanonicalJson, digestText, and Digestable; WHY: verifies the import wiring is in place

decision-doc-promotion.ts no longer defines normalizeJson, canonicalJson, digestCanonicalJson, or digestText locally (no function declarations for these names); WHY: verifies local duplicates were removed
computeDecisionDocProposalDigest on a pinned DecisionDocProposal returns the SAME hex digest as the pre-refactor version; WHY: the core behavioural invariant -- refactor must not change digest output

edge.desc: decision-doc-promotion.ts still exports computeDecisionDocProposalDigest, renderDecisionDocMarkdown, canonicalJson, digestCanonicalJson, digestText (re-exports or local); WHY: downstream consumers must not break due to missing exports
Digestable type is no longer defined in decision-doc-promotion.ts (it comes from core/digest.ts now); WHY: type duplication would cause maintenance drift

adversarial.desc: decision-doc-promotion.ts has no remaining import of node:crypto createHash (the digest logic is fully delegated to core/digest.ts); WHY: if createHash is still imported, the old inline code may be partially retained -- a mutation-detection signal

After refactor, calling digestDecision(decisionData, storyId) inside decision-doc-promotion.ts still works and produces same digest as before; WHY: digestDecision calls digestCanonicalJson internally, so import chain must be intact

items.title: Smoke + npm script + no regression (digest values identical, decision-doc behaviour unchanged)
items.context: tasks/experience-layer-digest-extract-smoke.ts + package.json test:experience-layer-digest-extract. Assert: digest functions byte-identical on pinned inputs; computeDecisionDocProposalDigest stable; existing decision-doc + experience-layer smokes still pass; build clean.
items.userSees: npm run test:experience-layer-digest-extract exits 0 'smoke passed'; committed verifier prints TOTAL N | PASS N | FAIL 0; existing decision-doc-related smokes still pass.

happy.desc: npm run test:experience-layer-digest-extract exits 0 and prints 'smoke passed'; WHY: the primary success gate for the smoke test
tasks/experience-layer-digest-extract-smoke.ts exists and is committed; WHY: the smoke must be a committed verifier, not ad hoc
Smoke verifier output shows TOTAL N | PASS N | FAIL 0 with N > 0; WHY: proves assertions actually ran (non-vacuous) and all passed

edge.desc: Existing decision-doc smoke (npm run test:decision-doc or equivalent) still passes after the refactor; WHY: regression guard -- the extraction must not break the original handler's test suite
tsc --noEmit (or npm run build) succeeds with zero errors; WHY: type-level regression guard -- the refactor must not introduce TS compilation errors
package.json contains the test:experience-layer-digest-extract script entry; WHY: the npm script wiring is part of the deliverable

adversarial.desc: Smoke test is non-vacuous: it contains at least one assertion that would fail if digest output changed (e.g., pinned expected hash compared to actual); WHY: a smoke that always passes regardless of implementation is useless -- must bind to real digest output
If core/digest.ts digestCanonicalJson were mutated to return a constant, the smoke would FAIL; WHY: mutation-proven non-vacuousness -- the test must actually detect implementation breakage
Smoke covers all three public functions (canonicalJson, digestCanonicalJson, digestText) with at least one assertion each; WHY: partial coverage would miss breakage in untested functions
